events.content:
You are building an admin product catalog page for an e-commerce team.

The catalog is read-heavy and should feel fast for day-to-day browsing, so avoid re-querying product data on every request.

Admins can trigger a "Sync latest catalog" action from the page when upstream ERP/PIM data changes (pricing, inventory, availability). After submitting, they should be able to continue working immediately, even if the product list is briefly stale.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.

events.content:
Done. The admin catalog page is live at `/admin/products`, builds cleanly, and renders all products plus the sync form (the non-zero exit above is just from killing the test server).

**What I built:**

- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `cacheComponents: true`, which turns on the `'use cache'` / `cacheTag` caching model in Next 16.
- **`lib/products.ts`** — the cached data layer. `getProducts()` uses `'use cache'` with `cacheTag('products')` and `cacheLife('max')`: since freshness is driven by the sync action's on-demand invalidation rather than a timer, entries stay warm and the DB isn't re-queried per request. Any other view that reads through this function shares the same `"products"` tag.
- **`app/admin/products/page.tsx`** — the catalog page with a plain HTML `<form>` whose `action` is an inline Server Action. The action calls `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — added a link to the admin page.

**The key design decision** is `revalidateTag('products', 'max')` rather than `updateTag('products')`. In this Next version those have opposite trade-offs: `updateTag` expires the cache entry immediately and blocks the action's response until fresh data is recomputed (read-your-own-writes), while `revalidateTag` with a cache-life profile marks the tag stale and returns immediately — readers keep getting the cached (briefly stale) list while every view tagged `"products"` refetches in the background. With sync jobs touching thousands of SKUs, blocking the admin on recomputation is exactly what the team wants to avoid, and the stale-while-revalidate path gives the requested eventual consistency across all catalog views.

In production, the Server Action body is also where you'd enqueue the actual ERP/PIM sync job before invalidating the tag — I left a comment marking that spot since there's no upstream to call in this stub.

Done. The admin catalog page is live at `/admin/products`, builds cleanly, and renders all products plus the sync form (the non-zero exit above is just from killing the test server).

**What I built:**

- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `cacheComponents: true`, which turns on the `'use cache'` / `cacheTag` caching model in Next 16.
- **`lib/products.ts`** — the cached data layer. `getProducts()` uses `'use cache'` with `cacheTag('products')` and `cacheLife('max')`: since freshness is driven by the sync action's on-demand invalidation rather than a timer, entries stay warm and the DB isn't re-queried per request. Any other view that reads through this function shares the same `"products"` tag.
- **`app/admin/products/page.tsx`** — the catalog page with a plain HTML `<form>` whose `action` is an inline Server Action. The action calls `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — added a link to the admin page.

**The key design decision** is `revalidateTag('products', 'max')` rather than `updateTag('products')`. In this Next version those have opposite trade-offs: `updateTag` expires the cache entry immediately and blocks the action's response until fresh data is recomputed (read-your-own-writes), while `revalidateTag` with a cache-life profile marks the tag stale and returns immediately — readers keep getting the cached (briefly stale) list while every view tagged `"products"` refetches in the background. With sync jobs touching thousands of SKUs, blocking the admin on recomputation is exactly what the team wants to avoid, and the stale-while-revalidate path gives the requested eventual consistency across all catalog views.

In production, the Server Action body is also where you'd enqueue the actual ERP/PIM sync job before invalidating the tag — I left a comment marking that spot since there's no upstream to call in this stub.
